title: Phased Upgrade Communication Playbook for Private Deployments
body:
Purpose:
This playbook provides a phased, tenant-aware communication approach and concrete message templates for SLA/SLO and maintenance window notices for private (VPC/on-prem) customers. It includes operator notes for Terraform module upgrades, rollback guidance, and pre/post upgrade validation checklists.

Audience:
- Customer technical contacts (admins/Platform teams)
- Customer legal/compliance contact (when required)
- Redwood account engineering / professional services contact
- Redwood SRE / release engineering / private deployments lead

Principles and constraints:
- Always offer a clear opt-out or reschedule path for customers on strict maintenance calendars (enterprise customers may require 30+ days notice).
- Assume limited cross-tenant orchestration visibility; communications should list exact impacts (API endpoints, control plane vs data plane).
- Keep messages short, actionable, and tokenizable (support variables like {{CUSTOMER_NAME}}, {{MAINT_START}}, {{MAINT_END}}, {{SRE_CONTACT}}).
- Respect customer-specified blackout windows captured in onboarding docs.

Phased communication cadence (recommended):
1) Pre-Announcement (business-level): 30 days for major breaking upgrades; 14 days for non-breaking but disruptive maintenance; 72 hours for minor patches that affect no contracts. Purpose: surface schedule, opt-out/reschedule policy, and high-level impact.
2) Technical Notice: 7 days (or 72 hours for smaller items). Include technical mitigations, rollback windows, and Terraform module change summary.
3) Reminder: 48 hours. Short note with links to runbook and support contact.
4) Final Reminder: 2 hours / 1 hour depending on SLA tier.
5) During Maintenance: short status messages at start and end, with progress notes for long windows.
6) Post-Maintenance: completion summary within 24 hours and post-mortem if SLOs were impacted.

Channels and recipients:
- Primary: email to customer admin distribution list (from redwood-ops@redwood.com)
- Secondary: dedicated Slack channel or customer-managed workspace integration when available
- Tertiary: PagerDuty/SMS for emergency rollback or immediate SLA breach notifications (pre-configured per contract)

Template tokens (required):
- {{CUSTOMER_NAME}}
- {{TENANT_ID}}
- {{MAINT_START}} (ISO8601)
- {{MAINT_END}} (ISO8601)
- {{IMPACT_SUMMARY}} (one line)
- {{SRE_CONTACT}} (name + email + pager)
- {{TF_MODULE_VERSION}}
- {{ROLLBACK_WINDOW}}

Sample messages (copy and adapt):
A) Business-level pre-announcement (30d):
Subject: Heads up: Planned Redwood Inference maintenance for your private deployment ({{MAINT_START}})
Hi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} team,
We plan a scheduled upgrade to your private deployment on {{MAINT_START}} (UTC). Expected window: {{MAINT_START}} to {{MAINT_END}}. High-level impact: {{IMPACT_SUMMARY}}.
If this window conflicts with your blackout dates or regulatory obligations, reply to this email within 10 business days to request an alternate window. Your Redwood account lead: {{SRE_CONTACT}}.
Thanks,
Redwood Private Deployments Team

B) Technical notice (7d):
Subject: Technical details & rollback plan — maintenance for {{TENANT_ID}} on {{MAINT_START}}
Hi,
This message lists the changes we will apply and what to expect: 
- Terraform module: redwood/private-deployments ({{TF_MODULE_VERSION}}) — bump includes VPC subnet numbering change and optional ipv6 flag.
- Expected downtime for control-plane migrations: up to 5 minutes per control-plane node; data-plane should remain available with degraded latency.
- Rollback availability: full rollback window until {{ROLLBACK_WINDOW}} after completion.
Pre-checks we will run: snapshots of local state, kube health checks (if applicable), KV-cache warmup.
Ops contact during maintenance: {{SRE_CONTACT}}.
If you run automated health checks, please expect transient 500s during the %%% pattern described in the runbook (link).

C) Friendly 48h reminder (short):
Subject: Reminder — maintenance for {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} on {{MAINT_START}}
Quick reminder: scheduled maintenance for your deployment in 48 hours. See full details: [runbook link]. Contact: {{SRE_CONTACT}}

D) Final 1h notice / go-live:
Subject: Start: maintenance window for {{TENANT_ID}} (starting now)
Maintenance has started. Impacts: {{IMPACT_SUMMARY}}. We will send periodic updates; expected final notice by {{MAINT_END}}.

E) Completion notice:
Subject: Complete: maintenance for {{TENANT_ID}} — success
Maintenance has completed at {{MAINT_END}}. Summary: upgrade to module {{TF_MODULE_VERSION}} applied; rollback not invoked. Key checks: control-plane health OK, token throughput at baseline +/-10%. If you observe issues, please reply to this thread and we will escalate immediately.

F) Failed/rollback notice:
Subject: Rollback executed for maintenance on {{TENANT_ID}}
We executed a rollback at {{ROLLBACK_TIME}} due to {{REASON_SHORT}}. Customer traffic was restored at {{ROLLBACK_COMPLETE}}. We will open a post-mortem and share next steps within 48 hours. Immediate mitigation: reverted Terraform to previous module version; checked DB migrations were not applied.

Operator runbook checklist (pre-upgrade):
- Verify latest tfstate is available and backed up to S3 (or customer-managed backend).
- Export customer-specific config: service accounts, KMS keys, whitelist ranges.
- Snapshot control plane & local databases (if applicable).
- Confirm monitoring & alerting (SLO dashboards accessible).
- Confirm contact list (email/pager/PD escalation) and blackout windows.
- Dry-run terraform (plan) with state lock and capture plan output.
- Smoke test harness: run 5 synthetic requests per region and confirm latency < 2x baseline.

Post-upgrade validation (immediate):
- Control plane convergence (all nodes Ready)
- API token issuance test (rotate a test token)
- End-to-end inference sanity tests (sample prompt -> expected responses)
- Embeddings index integrity checks for private index backends
- Cost/throughput sanity: token throughput within expected range

Terraform module notes (operator-facing):
- Breaking changes to call out explicitly in Technical Notice. Example: v1.0.0 renames variable vpc_subnet_count -> subnets_count (must coordinate with customer IaC).
- Always include module CHANGELOG snippet in the notice with migration hints.
- If module introduces optional feature flags (e.g., ipv6_enable), default to false unless customer requested.
- For private deployments, the module must never alter customer-defined CIDR blocks unless approved in writing.
- Verify provider and plugin versions (e.g., aws provider >= 4.20)
- Example upgrade steps (short): terraform init -> terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -> review plan with customer -> terraform apply with state lock -> post-apply verification scripts.

Escalation matrix (internal):
- Level 0: on-call private-deployments engineer (Slack @pd-oncall, PagerDuty).
- Level 1: Release engineering lead (Rosa Martinez).
- Level 2: SRE manager / account engineering (Maya Chen).
- Level 3: VP Eng for customer-impacting incidents.

Customer escalation path: Provide a single thread email + PD for immediate severity. Include opt-in SMS if contracted.

SLA/SLO communication guidance:
- If an SLO is at risk pre-upgrade, include that fact in the Technical Notice with mitigation steps. e.g., "We have identified a potential SLO drift risk for 99th latency during the first 30 minutes after restart; we will run a golden traffic set and monitor at 1-min granularity."
- If any SLO thresholds are crossed during maintenance, trigger the incident template and ensure post-maintenance retro and customer-facing post-mortem within 72 hours.

Optional templates for regulated customers (HIPAA/GDPR/FIN):
- Add legal/compliance cc list and include retention/backup location, KMS/HSM IDs used in the upgrade, and whether data left the customer's VPC.
- For air-gapped customers, include an explicit staging/validation step requiring customer sign-off before applying.

Notes to self / TODOs: (working list)
- Add runbook link once PD-Runbooks-PrivateUpgrades is finalized.
- Add terraform module migration table with diff examples (variable name changes, removed outputs).
- Draft customer-facing calendar invite template for 30d notices.
- Test templates in SendGrid sandbox and verify unsubscribe headers for compliance.

Appendix A: Example short technical checklist for customers to run (to be included in Tech Notice):
1) Validate network connectivity to control plane IPs in runbook.
2) Ensure service account used by Redwood has IAM roles: network:Read, kms:Decrypt (for customer-managed KMS), s3:GetObject for state snapshots.
3) Pause automated CI/CD runs against the deployment during maintenance window.

Appendix B: Example Terraform snippet to share with customers (one-line guidance, not code block):
- Recommend customers pin module versions in their root module: module "redwood_pd" { source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//private-deployments?ref=v1.0.0" }

End of draft.
Comments welcome — this doc is intentionally concise; expand into customer-specific versions (standard, regulated, enterprise) in follow-up drafts.
